source.title: Schrödinger's Bat: Diffusion Models Sometimes Generate Polysemous Words in Superposition

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether superposed prompt representations can produce multiple concepts and whether editing representations of ambiguous words changes generated senses, extending superposition-related work to Stable Diffusion and CLIP rather than testing the original toy-network setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own Stable Diffusion image-generation experiments. It also discusses results from Rassin et al. and Elhage et al.; those cited results are not recorded as rows. Figure-only image examples without separately described outcomes are not listed individually.
record.test_reason: The paper uses 'superposition' to mean a polysemous word's CLIP text embedding being a linear sum of sense vectors. It shows that summed prompt encodings yield both concepts in Stable Diffusion images, and that projecting out sense subspaces shifts the depicted sense. It does not test any version. There are no toy sparse-feature networks, no neuron polysemanticity or capacity allocation, and no LLM neuron-spread or SAE features. No test of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features is made either: the k<5 difference subspaces are a method choice, not a result. Near-orthogonality is offered as speculation, and is not measured. The capacity account (Section 6, citing Elhage et al.) explains DALL·E 2 vs Stable Diffusion differences without the authors' own data.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that summed CLIP encodings often yield images realising both prompts, and that sense-subspace editing substantially raises the targeted sense. They take this as support that polysemous-word encodings contain linear contributions from each meaning, and offer it as a plausible explanation of homonym duplication. They acknowledge the method is simplified and the directions approximate.
record.recipe_differences: The study manipulates CLIP text encodings and evaluates generated image contents; it does not reproduce the toy-network training setup or its feature-geometry measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary across prompt pairs and ambiguous-word prompts. The paper notes that some concept pairs yield hybrids or leakage rather than two cleanly represented concepts; sense-editing outcomes also depend on the prompt and target sense.

fits_no_version.finding: Averaging two CLIP prompt encodings (α=0.5) makes Stable Diffusion depict both concepts in 41.5% of images, significantly above the single-prompt baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distinct concept encodings in CLIP text space can be linearly summed with limited interference, so a downstream generator realises both concepts.

fits_no_version.finding: Projecting out an approximate sense subspace in CLIP's encoding of a polysemous word shifts which sense Stable Diffusion depicts, significantly for most prompt and sense pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Contextual embeddings of polysemous words contain approximately linear, separable sense components.

fits_no_version.finding: Similar concepts (cat+dog) yield hybrids rather than both objects. Attribute pairs (black/white cat, red/blue wall) show 'leakage' rather than two separate concepts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Summing encodings of similar concepts or attributes produces interference or blending rather than independent realisation.

record.problems: The paper says its sense directions are approximations based on a small number of handwritten sentences and that it edits only the ambiguous word, not other potentially relevant encodings. The method is demonstrated on Stable Diffusion rather than DALL·E 2. Most results use 30 images per condition; the reported significance tests do not provide effect-size intervals.
record.rows_left_out: No reported table results were left out. Individual figure-only image examples were not added as separate rows where the paper gives no distinct outcome statement or count.

untested.parts: No toy networks, sparsity sweep, phase transition, or feature geometry. Near-orthogonality of concept encodings is only speculated.
No neurons or capacity allocation are measured. The capacity explanation for DALL·E 2 vs Stable Diffusion is argued from citation, not tested.
No LLM neuron analysis or dictionary learning. The CLIP text-encoder sense directions come from handwritten contrast sentences, not sparse dictionary recovery.
Sense directions are single vectors derived from small subspaces, but 1-D versus multi-dimensional features are not compared.

missing.what: Aggregate over the selected prompt pairs: s1 only 35.2%, s2 only 20%, both 41.5%, neither 3.3%.
Qualitative failures: the cat+dog hybrid, and leakage for black/white cat and red/blue wall sums.

record.verdict_notes: 'Superposition' in this paper is linear sense mixture in an embedding (Arora et al. 2018 style), not features outnumbering dimensions. The Elhage et al. link appears only in the speculative Section 6. All 38 rows correctly carry versions ['none']. The study was not recorded as testing the claim, so no verdict labels are given.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, sparse features exceeding dimensionality, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular feature geometry are tested.
The study does not test neuron polysemanticity or capacity allocation between dedicated and shared dimensions.
It studies ambiguous word encodings and image generation, not polysemantic neurons or whether they arise without capacity pressure.
No LLM activations, neuron-spread measurements, or sparse autoencoder features are studied.
No SAE features or claims about their completeness, stability, or canonical status are tested.
The paper edits vectors and subspaces representing word senses, but does not test whether the features in superposition are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion
rows.operation_detail: Generated images from prompts containing polysemous words and observed homonym duplication for selected prompts.

conditions.value: selected examples, including cranes, bats, glasses, and bows

rows.measure: Whether images show multiple senses of a polysemous word
rows.value: The authors report successful replication of homonym duplication for some prompts; examples are shown in Figures 1, 2, and 7.
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: No frequency or denominator is given for these examples.
rows.check: These are selected qualitative examples with no denominator, and the authors say duplication is less frequent in Stable Diffusion. It is an existence observation only.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion
rows.operation_detail: Conditioned generation on the weighted sum of two CLIP prompt encodings, 0.5·CLIP(s1) + 0.5·CLIP(s2).
rows.measure: Generated-image content counts: s1 only / s2 only / both / neither
rows.uncertainty: p < 0.05; unpaired permutation test against the single-prompt generations
rows.note: The authors report that weighted sums for all tested pairs produced both concepts more often than either prompt alone, significantly.
rows.check: The prompt pairs were selected. Only pairs observed to realise both prompts are reported, and pairs that co-occurred too often were discarded. This applies to R2–R10.
